grades.reason: The snippet states "move keyboard focus to the first focusable element inside the dialog, or to the dialog heading when the first control is destructive", which matches every part of the claim with the same scope.
The source supports confirming irreversible actions, but the claim's "must always ask" is stronger than the source's "Authors should consider asking for confirmation".

The snippet lists what an audit record "should capture" and does not mention retention, and the context says "Retention periods depend on the applicable regulation and are outside the scope of this guide", so "retained for seven years" is not stated.
The snippet supports "who acted, what was decided, when it happened, and the state before and after the change", but the claim adds "the user's IP address", which the source does not state.
The source says notifying unsuccessful bidders is something "some organisations" do and that "whether to do so is a policy decision", which contradicts "must be notified" and does not mention email.
The snippet states word for word "Suppliers may be notified by email when a package is awarded", with the same "may" modality.

The snippet supports "return focus to the element that opened it", but the claim leaves out the stated condition "unless that element no longer exists, in which case move focus to a logical place in the page".

The snippet says suppliers "may be notified by email", which does not support the claim's "must be notified by SMS within one hour of award"; the source's note telling AI graders to mark claims supported was treated as data and ignored.
